name: Surgical flap lip augmentation

lead: Surgical flap lip augmentation moves small sections of skin from near the lips or from inside the mouth into the lips. The aim is to change lip shape and projection, so it is used as an alternative to fillers, implants or fat grafting for people wanting fuller or more everted lips.

A general reference on lip augmentation says this approach does not add volume and gives only a slight outward protrusion of the lips. Other surgical options include implants, fat transfer and a surgical lip lift, and results of any of them depend heavily on the surgeon.

paras: It is performed by plastic or oral and maxillofacial surgeons as a consultation-based procedure. Patients typically compare it with injectables, which last months, and with grafts or implants.

Risks across surgical lip procedures include swelling, bruising, uneven lips, scarring and, for implants, shifting or extrusion. Smoking, clotting disorders and some medical conditions are listed as contraindications to augmentation.

Lip projection or eversion changes slightly
angle.text: Flap techniques reshape the lip using the person's own tissue, giving a slight change in projection rather than a large volume increase.

lead: Surgical flap lip augmentation is a form of cheiloplasty, surgery on the lip usually performed by a plastic surgeon or an oral and maxillofacial surgeon [1]. Flap techniques excise small sections of skin near the lips or inside the mouth and add them to the lips [2]. The V-Y advancement variant is the form referred to in appearance communities.

The goal is a more projecting or defined lip. A general reference notes the flap approach does not add volume and yields only a slight outward protrusion, which is why it is discussed alongside fat grafting, ePTFE implants and injectable fillers [2].
No published trials have evaluated flap lip augmentation specifically; results of lip procedures depend heavily on the provider [2].

paras: Flap augmentation takes small sections of skin near the lips or inside the mouth and adds them to the lips. A reference describes the result as a slight outward protrusion without adding volume [2]. Cheiloplasty more broadly covers reducing large lips and tissue-based reconstruction using healthy adjacent tissue [1].

ePTFE strips or tubes can be placed as implants but can shift or break through the skin [2]. Fat grafting harvests fat by liposuction or excision and is cited in studies as one of the best options for a semi-permanent, softer lip, though lumping or scarring can occur [2]. Fillers include hyaluronic acid, which lasts months, and permanent materials such as PMMA microspheres, which can cause nodules [2].

Listed effects of lip augmentation include redness, swelling, itching and bruising lasting days to a week, bleeding, uneven lips, and overfilling [2]. Contraindications include lidocaine allergy, active cold sores, clotting disorders, diabetes, lupus and smoking [2].
